gaps.text: Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Low-level fusion: synchronized MIR ATR and fluorescence spectra from the same probe spot are concatenated into one matrix, with block scaling so neither method dominates. Both channels must sample the same small area and be normalized to a common time step. The fused model must beat the best single method on held-out samples, otherwise the extra channel is dropped.)

items.finding: Low-level data fusion rearranges data into a new matrix by placing variables from different sources one after the other.
items.how_it_applies: This approach could be tested to combine MIR ATR and fluorescence spectra, though instrument complementarity must be carefully evaluated first.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited review discusses general PAT applications rather than the specific biological tissues and optical configurations of this study.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
